title: The Jacket
full_review:
"The Jacket" (Warner Independent) is a dark and disjointed psychological thriller about an amnesiac Gulf War veteran (Adrien Brody) who is framed for the murder of a policeman and is sentenced to an asylum for the criminally insane.

Once institutionalized, the chief psychiatrist (Kris Kristofferson) subjects him to mind-altering "treatment" -- involving being strapped into a straitjacket and locked in a morgue body drawer -- which enables him to see the future, including his own imminent death.

While time-traveling, he also becomes romantically involved with a troubled waitress (Keira Knightley) whom he had helped as a girl in the past -- which is really the present. (Confused? Don't worry. You're not alone.) Knightley's edgy, mascaraed gal-pal role is the type usually played by Jennifer Jason Leigh, but here she's another doctor in the psych ward.

Stylishly crafted by director John Maybury, the creepy atmospherics fail to conceal that despite ending on a redemptive, life-affirming note the formulaic film lacks any real emotion or logic.

The film contains intense violence, including disturbing images of war, torture and a shooting; a sexual encounter with partial nudity; and recurring rough, crude and profane language. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is L -- limited adult audience, films whose problematic content many adults would find troubling. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted.
